steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Watch out! The Mania concentration here's off the charts!

Before your hand can rise, the alchemy cauldron brings its full weight down on the ground. The impact sweeps everyone off their feet and launches Lynn sideways. The gold coin slips loose again, spinning toward Murphy.

steps.speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
steps.content: Once I smelt it down... this false, twisted little world will tear itself apart!

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Oh no you don't!

EMP fires three explosive arrows straight at its core in rapid succession. But just before they reach the flames, the arrows lurch sideways as though seized by an invisible magnetic grip, spiraling off into crooked arcs. Then, a sickening sound of metal being chewed apart, and they disappear entirely.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: ...Did it just eat my arrows?! How are we even supposed to fight this thing?!
Letta tries to block with her lantern, but every impact pushes her closer to her limit.

steps.speaker: Letta
steps.content: Hmm... not working out too well, is it...

The alchemy cauldron has clearly lost its patience. It locks onto Murphy, huddled behind the rubble, closest to where the coin has landed. With a piercing shriek, several red-hot metal tentacles lash through the air like striking vipers, aimed straight for her chest.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Ah!
Murphy stares at the deadly crimson light closing in on her, her mind wiped completely blank.

In that split second, instinct takes over, and you throw yourself forward. The red-hot tentacle slices past your shoulder, opening a burning wound. You bite back a groan and wrap yourself around Murphy, using your own body as a shield.
The blow hurls both of you against the stone wall. A metallic tang rises in your throat.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Ch-Chief?! Blood... You're hurt?!

In an instant, Murphy's eyes go wide, and time itself seems to halt. She sees the way your brow tightens with pain, the dark crimson streaking down your uniform and splashing into the glowing melt below.
You swallow the fire tearing through your shoulder and unleash your shackles, seizing the coin still shivering with resonance.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Go show it... just how... unexpected the reality it wants can be.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: But... if I do this... will we even make it back to the Bureau?!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As long as we're breathing... we'll find a way!
Murphy shuts her eyes and hurls the coin high into the air—

steps.speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
steps.content: Futile! Let's see... what pathetic tricks you have left!

Murphy fixes her eyes on the shocking streak of red across your shoulder. Something in that cruel, vivid color cracks her final reserve of timidity wide open. The tears hovering in her eyes are gone in an instant, overtaken by a violent bloom of purple mist.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: You want it so badly... <color=#fb9259>then take it</color>!
The coin veers off at an impossible angle, bending every law of physics as it shoots cleanly into the alchemy cauldron.
By all rights, the cauldron should be roaring with laughter. But one loose screw is all it takes; its entire structure buckles and breaks apart right there.
It breaks down fast, even the metal arms it once took such pride in peeling off with it.

steps.speaker: Alchemy Cauldron
steps.content: No... this can't be real! My calculations were... foolproof...
A final, rage-filled scream rings out as the enormous alchemy cauldron slams to the ground.
One by one, the lights flicker to life. The lava-cave illusion rapidly peels away, revealing the cold metal framework of the Bureau's underground research facility.
But the contamination lingering in the air does not disperse. Mania still presses down on the underground levels, dense and cloying, an unshakeable gloom.

What lies beneath you now is no longer false brick and molten rock, but ruined conduits and sprawling crystalline formations of contamination, still radiating heat. An absurd dream, at last, with its skin torn open.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Emergency mode switch at fifty percent.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: What does "fifty percent" even mean?! When can you actually get in here? Chief is hurt!
As the interference fades, Nightingale's voice cuts back in. There's a rare edge of urgency in her tone.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief! Your condition... The Mania field hasn't been fully cleared yet. Please, stop all activity immediately and wait for external intervention! Do not go any further!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...I'm fine.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Chief...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Don't move, just stay still! The wound... the wound's still bleeding...
Murphy's hands scramble to cover the bleeding burn on your shoulder, frantic. But the instant her fingertips graze the wound, she snatches them back like she's touched fire.
This... this is all too familiar.
In that instant, the space around her—freshly restored to the Bureau's true form—bleeds into another memory: a stretch of blinding, sterile white.
[Hospital]

steps.speaker: Vague Voice
steps.content: ...It's okay. Just keep pressure on it.

steps.speaker: Vague Voice
steps.content: I'm not blaming you.

steps.speaker: Vague Voice
steps.content: It's just... I can't go back to how things were. Not thinking about anything.
See? As long as you stay by their side, things only get worse.
(Flashback)

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: No...

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: No... this isn't how it's supposed to go...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Murphy.
You start to speak, but she doesn't seem to register your voice. Her gaze stays fixed on the blood seeping from your shoulder.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: Hey. Don't you spiral on me now. Chief's still breathing!
Her hand retreats slowly. The trembling begins in her fingertips and spreads, reaching her shoulders before she can stop it.
You know better than anyone... People get close to you, they get hurt. Or worse.
It's always been like this. It's still like this.
How many more times are you going to watch it happen before you finally get it?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: As long as I'm here, it's just gonna keep getting worse.

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: Even the shackles won't be enough. Mania's getting stronger. It's only going to get more dangerous!

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I know everyone's been looking out for me... But...
Murphy hesitates. In the end, she can't bring herself to finish the sentence.
Looking out for you? No. They're paying the price for what should've been yours to carry.
The Chief bleeds today. What about next time?
Are you really going to wait until someone pays the full price in your place before you let go?

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: I can't stay with you all anymore.
Taking all the bad things on yourself... isn't that what you've always done best?
Just let go. I'll take all this misfortune off your hands. I'll deal with the mess. You'll never have to watch someone else bleed because of you again.
You... and your misfortune can't help anyone.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: What?! What kind of messed-up logic is that?! If you hadn't done what you did back there, we might not have been able to take down that pot—

steps.speaker: Murphy
steps.content: But Chief got hurt.
Her voice is so faint it hardly has any strength behind it, yet it hushes every other voice in the room.
She rises slowly as the words leave her. Those perpetually anxious eyes now hold yours, steady and unwavering, like she's finally arrived at a choice she's been running from for far too long.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: ...Do you really think walking away alone is going to fix everything?
Murphy says nothing. She offers a deep, respectful bow to everyone present, then climbs the Bureau stairs without a backward glance.
Right after, the analyzer Norma left behind blazes to life with searing red light.
The Mania fluctuations that had been dispersed across the entire area now converge at an alarming speed toward a single, narrow point.
You look up in the direction Murphy is walking. There's nothing there, but the shadows pooling on the floor continue to stretch, reaching further by the second.

steps.speaker: EMP
steps.content: ...Okay, I'm seeing that, right?

steps.speaker: Lynn
steps.content: Th-that's not Murphy's shadow...
Somewhere in the Bureau's lower depths, a laugh rings out, cold enough to freeze the blood in your veins.
Hehe...
Guess that big pot wasn't completely useless after all... The leftovers aren't exactly top-shelf, but... eh, I can work with it.
There, a shape that shares Murphy's every contour is voraciously feeding on the Mania left behind by the fallen alchemy cauldron.
Bureau members evacuate in controlled order under Nightingale's command, setting up a temporary command post just nearby.

Right now, she's locked onto the faint signal marking the Chief's coordinates. Just as the rescue passage into the Bureau is about to be forced open, the Mania field inside erupts in a violent second wave.
The buffer zone collapses, consumed in a heartbeat by the contamination's frenzied growth as it billows outward unchecked.
No time to call off the rescue team. Nightingale immediately reconnects with the Chief.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: I repeat, we're picking up a new core reaction! It's forming fast!

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Intensity—

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: —Intensity has already surpassed the previous peak!
From the deep shadows, the thing wearing Murphy's shape slowly opens its eyes.
As it raises its head, a monstrous grin stretches across its face.
There it is... all that effort wasn't for nothing after all.
You've finally come around, Murphy.
